recognize_zh: 低倍皮膚切片可見真皮全層被密集的結節狀淋巴球浸潤占據，並向下延伸至皮下，表皮本身未受侵犯；這種「由下而上」的結節狀、瀰漫性真皮浸潤是皮膚邊緣區淋巴瘤（MALT lymphoma）的低倍線索，但需高倍與免疫染色確認。
features: Dense, nodular to confluent lymphoid infiltrate occupying the full thickness of the dermis
Infiltrate extends into the deep dermis/subcutis as separate nodules
Epidermis is intact and not involved; a thin superficial dermal band appears relatively spared
Vaguely nodular pattern with paler areas suggestive of follicles or marginal zone expansion (not resolvable at this power)
Interstitial extension between collagen bundles at the periphery of the infiltrate
describe_en: Low-power H&E sections of a skin punch biopsy show a dense, nodular to diffuse lymphoid infiltrate involving the entire thickness of the dermis and extending into the deep dermis and subcutaneous tissue. The overlying epidermis is intact without epidermotropism. Cytologic detail and the composition of the nodules cannot be assessed at this magnification. In the appropriate immunophenotypic context, the architecture is compatible with cutaneous extranodal marginal zone lymphoma (MALT lymphoma).

ddx.vs: Reactive infiltrates are usually top-heavy with well-formed germinal centers and polytypic plasma cells, whereas MZL shows bottom-heavy expansion of marginal zone cells and light-chain-restricted plasma cells.

PCFCL shows follicular or diffuse centrocytes/centroblasts that are BCL6-positive, while MZL cells are small marginal zone/plasmacytoid cells that are BCL6- and CD10-negative outside colonized follicles.

CLL/SLL infiltrates are composed of monotonous small round lymphocytes with proliferation centers and a CD5+/CD23+ phenotype, unlike the CD5-negative mixed marginal zone/plasma cell population of MZL.

ddx.dx: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder
ddx.vs: This lesion is a CD4+ T-cell nodule with PD1+ follicular helper cells, whereas MZL is a CD20+ B-cell and clonal plasma cell infiltrate.
